description.description: Longer description of what this access policy governs.

layer.description: The access family's layer payload. Required when `type: 'layer'`, forbidden otherwise.

marking.description:
The whole marking of this access policy document, written in the scheme `marking_scheme` names. Every `marking` on one of its rules is a part of it.

Text, never interpreted: no engine parses it, checks it, or acts on it. The policy's summary reports it unchanged for display.

marking_scheme.description:
The scheme this document's markings are written in. An access policy is not a scheme, so it always names one by reference.

Authoring data only: no engine resolves the scheme it names.

rules.description: The policy's rules, evaluated in order.

target_scheme.description: The scheme whose markings this policy decides access to.

type.description: What kind of document this is. Absent means `'access'`. `type: 'layer'` requires the `layer` block and `type: 'access'` forbids it, both enforced at load. Every layerable family wears this same envelope; see `LayerBinding`.

version.description: Semantic version of this access policy.

vocabulary.description: Display words this policy advertises for UI consumers. A presentation hint only.

AccessCheckOperator.description:
How a check compares its operands.

- `is_in`: the left value is one of the right values.
- `contains_any`: the two sets share at least one value.
- `superset`: the left set holds every right value.
- `equals`: the two values are equal.
- `gte`: the left value is at or above the right one.
- `after`: the left value, a date and time, is later than the moment the   request is decided. It reads no right operand.

AccessGateOperator.description:
What a data gate asks of the data before a rule is evaluated.

- `has_concept`: the category holds the concept named in `value`.
- `has_content`: the category holds anything.
- `has_no_content`: the category holds nothing.
- `min_rank`: the category holds a concept ranked at or above `value`.

AccessLayer.description:
The access family's layer payload. Required when `type: 'layer'`, forbidden otherwise.

An access layer is complete-only, and this type is deliberately nothing but the binding. It has no `removes` and no `restores`, because there is no legitimate way for a layer to take away a mapping its base made: the two fields are absent so the refusal is in the shape, not only in the prose. The layer's own `rules` carry the additions, and a rule id that collides with one inherited from the base is a composition error the loader refuses, not an override that quietly wins.

The reason is authority, not tidiness. An organization holds concepts its parent structurally cannot know, and those concepts arrive through its own scheme layer, so mapping them to subject attributes is its own call to make. Everything the parent mapped stays the parent's. A child may complete what its parent could not know; it may not alter what its parent decided.

Binding is the cross-family one: see `LayerBinding`.

base.description: The artifact or layer this one stacks on, as `id@version`.

requires.description: Layers that must be present AND composed before this one. A layer that builds on what another layer introduced, or restores what another layer removed, only means anything on top of that layer, so the ordering is a load-time constraint rather than a hint.

AccessRule.description:
Strategy for comparing subject attributes against data assertions in a category during an access check.

- `gte`: user's ranked concept must be at or above the data concept's rank
- `superset`: user's concept set must include all data concepts
- `includes`: user's concept set must include at least one data concept
- `exact`: user's concepts must exactly match the data concepts

Declared on `AccessRuleDoc.strategy` for simple attribute-mapping rules.

AccessRuleCheckDoc.description:
A check that compares a subject attribute, a request context value, the data's concepts in a category, or a literal.

The left operand is `user`, or `context` when there is no `user`. The right operand is the first of `context`, `data_category` and `value` that is not already the left one.

context.description: Dot-path into the caller-provided request context.

data_category.description: A category whose concepts in the data are compared.

value.description: A literal compared against, when neither other operand is.

AccessRuleDoc.description:
One access rule as a policy authors it.

A simple rule maps a subject attribute onto a category: `attribute`, `category` and `strategy`. A check rule compares operands in a `check` block instead. Either may carry a data gate in `when`.

attribute.description: Simple rule: the subject attribute compared (a dot-path).

check.description: Check rule: the comparison it makes.

deny_reason.description: The reason given when this rule denies access. `{variable}` names a value the decision fills in.

marking.description: This rule's part marking, written in the scheme the document's `marking_scheme` names. Text, never interpreted: no engine parses it, checks it, acts on it, or reports it.

name.description: Human-readable name for this rule, shown in access decision output.

strategy.description: Simple rule: how the attribute is compared with the data's concepts in `category`. Required with `attribute`; a check rule does not read it.

values.description: Simple rule: maps attribute values onto concept ids.

view.description: Simple rule: the concept view the attribute's values are written in.

when.description: Evaluate the rule only when the data passes this gate.

AccessRuleGateDoc.description: A data gate: the rule is evaluated only when this holds of the data.

operator.description: What the gate asks of the category.

value.description: A concept id for `has_concept`, a rank for `min_rank`.

MarkingSchemeRefDoc.description: The scheme a document's markings are written in, named by id and, optionally, version. Every document that can be marked names one this way; a scheme document may also write `self`. See `SchemeBlock.marking_scheme`.

version.description: The marking scheme's version. Omitted, any version.

SchemeDependencyDoc.description: A scheme another document depends on: the scheme a guide's outcomes, an access policy's rules, or one side of a crosswalk are written in.

version.description: The scheme version, or a semver range such as `>=2.0.0`. Omitted, any version.

term.description: A singular and plural display-word pair, as a document declares it.

plural.description: The word for more than one, such as `rules`.

singular.description: The word for one, such as `rule`.

vocabulary.description: Display words a document advertises for UI consumers: an open map from a term key (such as `rule` or `concept`) to its words. A presentation hint only; no engine reads it.

description: Top-level YAML document for an access policy. This is the published 1.0 document format; the runtime `AccessPolicy` is the engine's resolved in-memory shape after loading and is not part of the published contract.
